content_of_post_to_comment:
I wake up at 5am and go to sleep at 7:30pm.

My energy level is on a whole new level for the last 7 months.

And what's even more awesome is I don't have sleep issues anymore because once 7:30pm comes around, my body automatically becomes sleepy.

I just have consistent energy throughout my day and week. No highs and lows.

I don't use any caffeine or tea.

I used to take a 1 hour nap every single day, not anymore.

At first I tried 5am wakeup and 8:30pm sleep but ended up taking lots of naps on the weekends which meant I had sleep debt.

I implemented many tips from r/productivity but this is the #1 change that I made by far.

Evening timing= Dinner is finished by 6pm.

Morning routine= half glass of water drink and then 3 min jumprope with cordless jumprope. Use a physical alarm clock and not my smartphone.

For those who shifted to an early bed schedule, what specific evening boundaries did you have to put in place to protect your wind-down time?
comment: The dinner cutoff is probably doing more work than people realize. I had a similar shift when I stopped treating evenings as extra productivity time and started protecting the last couple hours before bed. The hard part wasn't waking up early, it was saying no to late meals, screens, and random “one more thing” tasks. Did you find your social life had to change much with a 7:30pm bedtime?
